note: hand labels (Claude reading, 2026-10-17): placement = names a separate thing the object rests on/leans against/hangs from/lies on/is fastened to/points toward (page staging); built-in parts are NOT placement. Only the keyword candidates were read; the rest are unlabelled.

candidates.desc: Type: ancient celestial navigation device. Description: round brass compass the size of a pocket watch, carved with constellation patterns around the rim, central crystal that glows blue-white when active, three interlocking rings that rotate, back engraved with Costa Rican indigenous symbols, attached to a braided leather cord
Large rectangular flag, white background with red cross of Castile, gold castle emblems, attached to wooden pole

An old white porcelain bathtub mounted on a wooden frame with four antique wooden wheels with metal rims. The wheels have different carved patterns in the spokes. A yellow carved duck bill extends from the front as a nose, and white painted wooden wings are attached to both sides. The whole construction looks absurd but charming, with visible brass screws and a simple steering wheel mounted inside the tub.
A golden trophy shaped like a small soap box racer with wings extending from both sides, mounted on a dark wooden base with an engraved plaque reading 'Das Grosse Rollen - Kreativität & Teamgeist'.

a thick weathered tree trunk lying horizontally across the full width of the forest path, bark grey-brown and mossy, diameter roughly as tall as a preschool child; the root mass rises at the left end, a tangle of dark roots and clods of earth; broken branch stubs protrude from the upper surface at irregular intervals

a child-sized bicycle with a blue painted steel frame, two equal-sized black rubber wheels, straight handlebars, a small black saddle, no training wheels; on page 6 Max sits astride it coming to a stop; on page 7 it lies on its side on the forest path beside the fallen tree

a small cylindrical plastic water bottle with a red screw-top cap, semi-transparent with water visible inside; on page 6 it is clipped to a holder on the bike frame at hip height; on page 7 it lies among the thorn stems at the edge of the thicket, partially hidden

a small rectangular picture book, roughly A5 size, with a thick card cover in warm red; the cover face carries blurred colour illustration marks with no legible text; on page 9 it lies open face-up across Kiaan's lap; on page 11 it is closed and tucked under Kiaan's arm

a small square fabric bag in dark blue cotton with a drawstring pulled tight at the top; roughly the size of a lunchbox; on page 9 it sits closed on the bench beside Kiaan; on page 10 it hangs from Kiaan's shoulder; on page 11 it sits open on the ground, the drawstring loosened so the top opening is visible

three large curved shell fragments of rough granular texture matching the speckled brown-and-cream pattern of the whole egg, each roughly palm-sized, lying scattered among the tree roots with the concave inner surface facing upward on two and the outer surface on one

Large paper map of the North Atlantic pinned to a pale cream bedroom wall. Dotted pencil line from New York to Paris with seven small circles. Surrounding the map are pinned newspaper clippings in black-and-white, cut unevenly, with visible bold headlines. A small tin of pencils sits on the desk below.
Black steel frame, wide handlebars, brown leather saddle, leaning against a wooden fence post on a residential street visible through the staircase window.
small wooden cage with reed bars, rope closure knot, sits on sandy ground

A fallen tree branch lying horizontally across the muddy forest path foreground; roughly the diameter of a child's wrist; bark is dark brown-grey and slick with rain, patches of green-grey lichen along one side; length spans roughly two adult arm-spans

A full tree trunk lying horizontally, spanning the full width of the stream from bank to bank; trunk diameter is roughly level with a small child's knee; bark is dark brown-grey, soaked through and slick with rain-wet sheen rendered in watercolor washes; the surface is uneven with a few broken branch stubs along its length; both ends rest on the stream banks with the mid-section sitting only a hand's-width above the moving water surface

A row of four flat rounded stones set in a line across the stream, each roughly the width of a child's foot; all four are fully submerged under brown-tinted moving water so only their dark rounded shapes are faintly visible beneath the surface; water ripples and eddies visibly above them

A tall stone column rising from a wide shallow circular stone basin at ground level; the column is rough-hewn warm grey limestone; a small bronze figure stands at the very top of the column; the basin rim is broad enough to sit on and shows dark watercolor-wash weathering stains along its sides; the whole structure stands roughly twice the height of an adult

Rectangular glass-topped cases with dark wooden frames, each roughly waist-high on an adult; arranged in a loose row in the garden; inside each case pale cream-coloured fossil bone shapes rest on dark grey fabric; the glass tops reflect pale sky in watercolor washes

A rectangular wooden-framed information board standing upright on two short posts set into the ground. The board face is approximately twice as wide as it is tall. The wooden frame is weathered brown. The board face shows a painted illustration of a dragon in flight above mountain peaks with small orange dot clusters on the peak tops; all text on the face is weathered and illegible. The board stands at roughly adult chest height.

Small clusters of warm orange glow sitting on the silhouetted ridgelines of distant high Alpine peaks. Each cluster is a soft irregular patch of deep amber-orange light, roughly the apparent size of a fingertip at distance, with a gentle diffuse halo. Multiple clusters are spaced apart across two or three separate peaks.

A large fallen tree trunk lying horizontally across a narrow forest stream, spanning the full width. The trunk is roughly as thick as a young child's torso. The bark is dark grey-brown and mossy, the surface uneven with occasional knots and short broken branch stubs. The top surface is slightly flattened from weathering.

forearm-length stock of dark oiled walnut wood, iron prod (bow) spanning about half an arm's width, hemp string, a simple iron nut-and-lever trigger; two iron-tipped wooden bolts carried in a flat brown leather quiver strapped to Roger's back
a fist-sized apple with bright red skin and a short brown stem; in Page 4 it appears split cleanly in two, the pale yellow flesh visible, lying on grey cobblestones
massive stone fireplace built into wall, large enough to stand in, burning logs, iron grate, smoke rising to chimney

A palm-length toy sword carved from pale blonde wood, roughly 40 cm total. A straight flat blade approximately 30 cm long and 3 cm wide, with a simple rounded D-shaped wooden hand guard and a short cylindrical grip wrapped in brown twine. No sharp edges; the tip is rounded. Light enough to hang from a rope belt loop.

Five circular medallions, each the size of a large coin. Lukas has golden, Manuel has crimson red, Franziska has bronze-gold, Sophie has silver with turquoise edge, Roger has deep blue. Each has raised geometric patterns and glows when activated. Hung on simple leather cords.
A chunky, hand-painted red-and-white wooden sailing boat about 30 cm long, with a white cotton sail and a tiny painted porthole on each side. Worn from play, with a small rope tied to the bow.

an arm-length rectangular wooden chest — dark brown aged oak planks with visible wood grain, held together by four rusted iron bands running horizontally across the lid and body; a small rusted iron hasp and padlock clasp at the front center; the iron fittings are rough and pitted with orange-brown rust; a small iron keyhole is set in the hasp; when open, the lid stands at roughly a right angle to the body, hinged at the back with two iron hinges

a finger-length iron skeleton key, dark grey with surface rust spots, with a small round bow (ring top) and two short rectangular teeth at the bit end; slightly bent from age; hangs from a short loop of rough hemp twine

A tall straight wooden pole approximately two metres high, planted in the center of the Altdorf market square. On top sits a broad-brimmed dark grey felt hat with a short black feather tucked into a dark band.
A dark blue city bicycle with a black handlebar, a narrow black seat, and silver spokes. Standard adult-size frame. No basket. A dark green bike helmet hangs from the handlebars when parked.

a rounded dark grey felt hat mounted on a carved wooden bracket near the top of a tall straight wooden pole; the pole is rough-hewn pine, approximately the height of two adults; the hat sits level on the bracket, its round crown visible from a distance; the bracket is a simple horizontal wooden peg
a medium-sized dark navy blue child's rucksack with two padded shoulder straps and a front zip pocket with a small white FCZ logo patch sewn on; lying flat on a pale wooden floor
a single dark grey adult sneaker with a white rubber sole and white laces, lying on its side on a pale wooden floor

a pale blue chalk arrow drawn directly on the pale grey cobblestone surface of the Rathausbrücke bridge; the arrow is roughly forearm-length, pointing toward the right, with a single line shaft and a triangular arrowhead; the chalk is slightly worn but clearly visible against the grey stone

a large silver stainless steel cooking pot with two black riveted side handles, roughly the size of a football in diameter and half-football in height, sitting on a kitchen hob ring with its lid leaning against it

a tall rough-hewn wooden pole, approximately twice a man's height, with a plain dark wool cap fixed to the top — the cap is rounded, dark grey-brown, with a simple narrow brim, pinned in place with a leather cord
a fist-sized bright red apple, smooth-skinned with a short brown stem; on Page 3 it sits balanced on Lukas's head; on Page 4 it lies in two clean halves on the cobblestones, white interior visible

A forearm-length (approximately 25 cm × 12 cm × 10 cm) rectangular box made of dark walnut-brown wood with a smooth lacquered surface. On the left short side, a small round brass button is set into the wood. An identical small round brass button is set into the right short side. The lid is hinged at the back and held shut by the two buttons — it swings open upward when both are pressed simultaneously. The interior is lined with pale cream-coloured fabric.

A fist-sized blue-painted metal toggle lever mounted on a small wall panel in Section C. The lever moves between a DOWN position and an UP position. In the DOWN position the lever body hangs at roughly 45 degrees downward; in the UP position it stands nearly vertical. The panel background is grey aluminium with a simple direction label above.

a palm-length silver metal lever mounted vertically on the dark grey plastic dashboard of the fire engine cab, with a round black rubber grip at the top; the lever sits in a slotted chrome bracket with a spring return mechanism visible at the base

a bright yellow hard-plastic firefighter helmet — a rounded dome-shaped shell with a wide brim all around, a black foam inner liner visible at the rim, and a red firefighter emblem decal on the front; hung on a metal wall peg

a thick orange rubber fire hose, arm-diameter, coiled in a flat circle roughly two forearms in diameter and wound into three parallel loops, hung on a large round steel wall hook; the hose ends are sealed with chrome brass coupler fittings

a large industrial gas cylinder — forearm-thick steel tube roughly waist-tall, painted gunmetal grey with a round chrome valve fitting at the narrow top end and a flat steel base at the bottom; lying on its side on concrete floor in pages 11-12, upright in page 15

a polished brass bell, roughly the size of two fists, with a deep curved bell body and a cast iron clapper inside; mounted on an iron bracket on top of a short weathered oak wooden post sunk into the courtyard; a thick braided natural-fibre rope of arm-thickness and roughly body-height hangs from the iron bracket down to waist level for pulling

A straight wooden pole approximately two metres tall, driven into the cobblestones of the Altdorf marketplace. At the very top, Gessler's wide-brimmed velvet hat with a long ostrich plume is mounted on a wooden peg, clearly visible at eye level above the crowd. The pole is unadorned raw timber, the hat alone marking it as the seat of authority.

A wide rough-planked wooden medieval rowboat approximately four metres long, with high squared gunwales, two iron oarlocks set into the upper rail on each side, two long wooden oars with flat paddle blades, a wooden stern tiller post for steering, and unpainted dark-weathered timber planks. The boat has no mast or sail — oar-powered only.

A wide-brimmed velvet hat with a long ostrich plume — the hat of authority placed on a pole in Altdorf marketplace by the Vogt (governor) Gessler, who demanded that every passer-by bow before it. The hat is dark wine-red velvet with a stiff wide brim and a single long white-grey ostrich feather curving up from the band. It sits atop a wooden pole.
a single dark blue children's lace-up sneaker lying on its side on pale laminate floor; white rubber sole, velcro strap undone, size roughly 20 cm long

four white ceramic dinner plates each roughly 25 cm diameter, four clear glass tumblers, and four stainless-steel forks laid on a light wooden dining table; items partially placed and partially still being arranged

a small round ceramic bowl, palm-sized (roughly 8 cm diameter), in solid blue glaze, sitting on the kitchen windowsill beside the terrarium; filled with clear water. Accompanied by a standard transparent 500 ml plastic water bottle with a white screw cap

a large silver stainless-steel cooking pot approximately 30 cm in diameter, sitting on a black ceramic stovetop burner, filled with bubbling deep-red tomato sauce; a long wooden cooking spoon (roughly 35 cm) rests inside the pot with the handle leaning against the rim; steam rises from the surface

two round lollipops each roughly the size of a large coin (5 cm diameter), individually wrapped in shiny red cellophane twisted at the top around a thin white paper stick approximately 10 cm long; one is held in a child's hand, the other still sits in the open wooden box

A vertical wooden post roughly chest-height on an adult, natural mid-brown wood with a slightly weathered grain; two horizontal rectangular yellow-painted wooden sign arms attached at right angles to the post at different heights, each pointing in a different direction; the text on the arms is illegible at illustration distance; the post base is planted in the ground

A traditional Swiss alpine gate: two vertical dark-brown weathered wooden posts planted in the ground roughly shoulder-width apart on a mountain path, connected by three horizontal dark-brown wooden rails spanning parallel across the gap; a simple iron latch bar rests in an iron hook on the right post, holding the gate closed; the gate swings inward on two iron hinges on the left post

A squat rectangular chest carved from pale grey granite, roughly knee-height and arm-span wide, resting on the flat summit rock; its lid is a single flat slab of the same pale grey granite, slightly overhanging the body on all sides; on page 13 the lid is open a finger-width showing a warm shimmer of green inside; on page 14 the lid is fully open resting against the back face of the chest

A round rubber ball slightly smaller than a child's fist, solid blue in colour, with no markings or patterns; on page 1 it sits in the front basket of Julian's Velo; on page 9 it remains inside Julian's backpack, the round bulge visible through the fabric

A red child's bicycle sized for a preschool child, with two wheels, a low step-through frame, a padded red saddle, straight handlebars with red rubber grips, a small front basket mounted on the handlebars, and no training wheels; the frame is a single dominant red colour with no visible decals

The Lunar Module Eagle's front descent ladder — a vertical aluminium structure about two metres tall attached to the front leg of the module, with nine horizontal rungs spaced evenly apart between two parallel vertical side rails. The ladder leads from the module's front hatch down to a circular foot-pad at the base. The module body behind it is covered in gold foil and silver panels.

A standard American flag — a rectangle of red, white, and blue with white stars on blue in the upper-left corner and alternating red and white horizontal stripes — mounted on a metal flagpole pressed into the lunar dust. A horizontal wire runs along the entire top edge of the flag, holding it fully extended and rigid in the airless environment, so the flag appears frozen mid-wave. The flagpole is silver metal, approximately one and a half metres tall.

A boxy 1960s black-and-white television set approximately 50 centimetres wide and 40 centimetres tall, mounted on a metal stand at approximately seated eye-level. The screen is a convex rectangle showing a grainy grey-toned image of a white-suited figure on a pale surface. Two rabbit-ear antennae extend from the top rear corners of the set. The cabinet is dark grey plastic with a round tuning dial on the lower right front panel.

A coil of thick natural-fibre rope approximately 40 cm in diameter and 15 cm tall when laid flat, the rope itself about 3 cm thick. The colour is warm straw-yellow. The coil rests in a loose spiral of approximately eight loops. The rope surface shows a twisted three-strand weave.

A loose gathering of round flat coins each approximately 3 cm in diameter and 3 mm thick. The colour is warm yellow-gold. The coin surfaces show faint relief markings that are weathered and illegible. The coins sit in a shallow pile inside the chest and in two separated groupings on the stone beside it.

A large hardcover book approximately 35 cm tall and 25 cm wide, lying open flat on a reading stand. The cover boards are dark brown leather with worn edges. Both pages visible are covered in dense columns of small printed text in black ink, the individual words illegible at reading distance. The back inside cover pocket, visible at the lower right when the book lies open, holds the folded map — one amber-brown corner of paper protrudes about 3 cm above the pocket edge.

A single-masted wooden sailing vessel approximately 15 metres long with a broad hull. The hull planks are dark brown with a single wide yellow painted stripe running along the full length at the top of the hull, just below the rail. The name GOLDENE MÖWE is painted in yellow block letters on the dark brown bow. One tall wooden mast rises from the centre of the deck. A single large square sail hangs from a horizontal wooden yard: the sail is white cotton with a painted black silhouette of a flying seagull at its centre. The deck planks are unpainted grey-brown wood. A wooden ship's wheel with eight spokes stands at the stern. A narrow wooden gangway plank connects the port side midship rail to the riverbank when moored. The stern carries a small carved wooden gull figure as a figurehead on the transom.

A single large scale roughly the size of an open adult hand, oval in outline with a pointed tip at the bottom and a slightly curved flat top edge where it once attached to the wing. The surface carries the same deep forest-green base colour as the dragon's body with ochre-gold undertones that catch warm light. The texture is smooth with faint concentric ring markings pressed into the surface. The edges are slightly translucent at the very rim in a warm amber wash. No metallic shine — rendered in warm watercolour pigment.

A rectangular flat plank of rough-hewn pale brown timber mounted horizontally on a single vertical wooden post. The post is driven into stony ground. The plank face shows a row of five simple symbols carved into the wood — geometric shapes including a circle, a triangle, two parallel horizontal lines, and a cross — arranged left to right in a single row. No letters or numbers appear on the sign. The carved symbols are dark-shadowed against the lighter wood grain.

a single rough-hewn wooden post planted vertically in the ground with three flat rectangular wooden arm boards attached horizontally at the top, each arm pointing in a different direction — left, centre and right; the arms are unpainted weathered pale brown timber; each arm has weathered carved text that is illegible at reading distance; the post stands at chest-height to a preschool child

a low rectangular chest carved from pale grey granite, roughly knee-height to an adult, as wide as two children standing side by side; a flat slab lid rests on top when closed; the lid is hinged at the back with two visible dark iron bands; the outer surface is rough-hewn with visible chisel marks; no lock visible on the exterior; no text

a low gate spanning a narrow path, made of two vertical rough timber planks connected by two horizontal cross-rails — one near the top, one near the bottom — forming a simple rectangular frame; the gate swings on two dark iron strap hinges fixed to a timber post on the left; the top cross-rail has words carved along its length in shallow chisel cuts that are illegible at viewing distance; the gate stands open, swung to the right, with the path visible beyond

a tall stone pedestal topped by a seated bronze-coloured figure of a bearded man in 19th-century frock coat, the figure facing forward with one hand resting on the knee; the pedestal is pale grey granite with moulded base and cornice; a shallow circular basin surrounds the base at ground level; warm ochre and grey washes describe the stone; the whole monument stands roughly three adult heights tall

A carved rectangular stone panel set into the front face of the fountain basin, approximately forearm-length wide; it depicts a simple heraldic shield with a diagonal band carved in low relief, worn smooth by weather.

A hand-bound book approximately A5 size with a soft cream fabric cover decorated with small hand-drawn flowers in pencil; its pages are filled with printed photographs and handwritten captions in blue ink; lying open on a stone surface.

a chest-height stack of round split birch logs, pale cream-white wood faces visible, stacked neatly in a rectangular formation approximately one metre wide and one metre tall, set on bare packed earth
a fist-sized dented grey tin metal bucket with a single arched wire handle, lying on its side on the grass, worn and scratched
a silver mid-size family sedan with four doors, round headlights, a pale grey dashboard inside, child seat mounted on the rear passenger side, simple and modern styling
a mid-sized dark blue school backpack with yellow zipper pulls and two front pockets, lying on a wooden floor
irregular pale grey cobblestones set in fan-shaped patterns on a narrow lane or bridge surface, slightly worn smooth from centuries of foot traffic, warm summer light catching the rounded stone edges

a wooden sailing boat roughly ten metres long with a single mast rising from the centre of the deck; the hull is dark brown painted wood sitting low in the water; a large square-cut sail is rigged on a horizontal yard mounted at right angles to the mast and hangs from it, the sail fabric cream-white with a simple black painted shape of crossed bones at its centre; the bow is blunt and rounded; a rope railing runs along each side of the deck attached to short wooden posts; the stern has a flat rail where a figure can stand at the tiller

The lowest step of a wooden residential staircase — a broad flat wooden tread with a rounded front edge, painted white on the riser, the tread itself in pale natural wood, wide enough for an adult to sit on comfortably

A single-scoop ice cream cone — the scoop is large and dark brown chocolate, roughly fist-sized, sitting on a pointed waffle cone that is forearm-length from tip to scoop; the top of the scoop has a small bite taken out of it

A single-scoop ice cream cone — the scoop is pale rose-pink strawberry, roughly fist-sized, sitting on a pointed waffle cone forearm-length from tip to scoop; the surface of the scoop is smooth and slightly glistening

A child's palm-sized LED headlamp: a narrow rectangular white plastic casing mounted on a thin elastic orange band worn around the forehead; a single bright white LED lens centered in the front face; emits a focused narrow cone of white light

a double-winged aircraft of wood and off-white muslin fabric: two flat rectangular wings stacked one above the other, the lower wing slightly wider, spanning about 12 metres; a small gasoline engine mounted on the lower wing surface near the center, connected by chain-drive to two pusher propellers mounted behind the wings; no wheels — rests on a wooden launch rail; the pilot lies prone on the lower wing surface at the center; the entire frame is lightweight spruce wood with muslin fabric pulled taut over it

a wooden launch rail made of six flat wooden planks laid end-to-end on the sand, forming a straight track roughly 18 metres long and 15 cm wide, slightly raised above the sand surface on wooden supports; the planks are smooth and straight, and a small wheeled wooden dolly sits at the starting end ready to carry the aircraft forward

a simple rectangular wooden writing desk, roughly 120 cm wide and 70 cm tall, with two drawers on the right side, a plain flat surface, and turned wooden legs; the wood is dark stained; a small inkwell sits in the upper left corner of the surface

a white wax candle, roughly 15 cm tall and 2 cm in diameter, nearly burned down to 3 cm, set in a flat circular brass candleholder with a short finger-ring handle; the flame is small and flickering, producing a small pool of warm yellow light

An egg roughly the size of a football, oval with a slightly blunter top end. Surface is covered in irregular faceted scales the colour of warm grey-green stone, with fine dark veining between each scale. On page 1 the whole egg glows from within with a steady warm amber light that softens the edges of the scales. On page 2 the shell lies in two or three large broken pieces on the forest floor, inner surface smooth and cream-coloured, outer surface still showing the scale texture.
A standard-size football with a classic black-and-white panel pattern. Rests on the forest path on its own, partially visible behind the trees where it was left behind.

A large tree trunk, roughly as wide as a child's shoulders, lying horizontally across a muddy brook. Bark surface is dark brown-grey with patches of pale green moss. The log spans the full width of the water, both ends resting on muddy banks. Surface is slightly uneven with a few broken stub branches.

A small child's bicycle scaled for a five-year-old — frame roughly 60 cm long, saddle height around 45 cm. The frame is bright red with a wide curved top tube. Two black rubber wheels with knobby tread. A straight handlebar with short black rubber grips. A small silver bell mounted on the left side of the handlebar. A dark grey fabric saddlebag loops over the rear rack.

A tall black cast-iron post about three times the height of an adult, topped with a single globe lantern of frosted pale glass enclosed in a simple black iron frame, mounted on a flared base bolted to the stone paving; the lamp is lit, casting a warm amber circle on the wet cobblestones below.

a small carved jack-o'-lantern carried by a sturdy curved wire handle attached to its rim, glowing constantly from within with warm orange light; perfectly round orange ribbed shell with a simple friendly face cut into it
A short child's cape in deep purple velvet, reaching to the knees, with golden moons and stars embroidered along the hem and collar; fastens at the throat with a small golden clasp

a roughly thumb-sized figure shaped from grey modelling clay: a round head with a pressed-in visor line, a rectangular body, two stubby arms held wide, standing on a flat base; uneven but clearly recognisable as a knight in armour
a small wooden toy car with a curved roofline, four thick rounded black wooden wheels mounted on silver metal axles, and bright red paint on the main body with no lettering or text
a round bucket built from vertical pale pine wood staves held together by two dark iron hoops, featuring a thick carved wooden handle attached to the top rim
A miniature brown leather riding saddle with a curved seat, thick stitching, and small metal stirrups hanging from the sides.
a brass hand bell with a domed bell body, a loop handle on top, and a clapper hanging from the inside of its mouth, its rim a plain polished edge
a pair of reading glasses with two round lenses set in thin black plastic frames joined by a short bridge, with black temple arms
A brass ship lantern with a ring handle over its domed cap, a square cage of brass bars around a clear glass chimney, and a flat brass base, hung from a bail at the top.

a small square lantern about the size of a child's fist, made of dark iron with four flat glass panes set into the four sides; a short iron ring at the top for hanging; the glass glows warm amber-yellow when lit; the iron frame is matt black with visible surface texture.

a single thick iron hook curved at ninety degrees and fixed to the wooden post beside the ship's wheel; the hook is matt black iron, roughly the length of a hand, with a blunt tip and a flat mounting plate nailed to the wood.

A round-crowned hat with a wide flat brim all around; warm tan canvas fabric, slightly dusty and bent at the front brim from handling; no insignia; on page 1 it hangs on a wooden fence post by its brim, on page 6 it lies in long grass

A roughly oval fieldstone about as wide as a child's two hands placed side by side; white to pale grey in colour, smooth on top, flat on the bottom; sits at the base of a stone barn wall; shown already displaced, lying beside its original hollow in the ground

a single sheet of off-white paper roughly the size of an open picture book, edges slightly uneven and tea-brown at the tips from age, rolled into a tight cylinder and held by a thin brown cord when closed; when open it lies flat with gentle curl at the side edges, covered in smudged and weathered markings across its face

a large rectangular woven blanket, about the size of a single bed sheet, in wide alternating red and white stripes running along its length, edges finished with a simple hem, laid flat on the ground with mild surface creasing

a circular steering wheel mounted on a vertical post fixed to the deck, roughly chest-high on a small child, dark brown painted wood, eight evenly spaced straight spokes radiating from a central hub to the outer rim, rim diameter wide enough that a small child must stretch both arms to reach opposite handles, the whole wheel sitting perpendicular to the deck surface

a child-scale play ship constructed from large panels of brown corrugated cardboard, painted over in uneven cream and grey-brown tones with visible brush marks; the hull rises to roughly adult shoulder height with a raised rectangular stern section at the back and a lower bow at the front; a single tall vertical mast of painted cardboard tubing rises from the deck centre, a rectangular white cotton sail hanging from a horizontal crossbar lashed near the top — the sail hangs slack with slight sag at its lower edge; a short bowsprit pole juts forward from the bow at a shallow upward angle; the deck is a flat platform of cardboard with irregular plank-line markings painted across it; the fixed wheel post rises at the stern end of the deck; the near-side rail is a single horizontal cardboard strip running at hip height on a small child, supported by three evenly spaced vertical posts; a second lower rail runs along the far side of the ship at the same height; the whole structure sits directly on the grass with no wheels or supports visible

a large sheet of aged parchment, roughly rectangular and about as wide as two open hands placed side by side, with irregular deckled edges and several small tears along the margins; the surface facing the viewer is the plain back of the sheet — pale cream-yellow, fibrous, mottled with faint water stains and darkened creases; the sheet lies flat, not rolled

a flat iron cleat bolted to the surface of the deck boards, two short horizontal horns projecting outward from a central upright body, the whole piece about as wide as an open hand; the iron is dull grey-black with spots of rust at the bolt heads; the working rope is wound in a figure around both horns and runs taut off the edge

a two-masted wooden sailing vessel with a hull painted deep gold-yellow below the rail and dark brown at the waterline; the hull planking shows visible caulked seams; the bow rises to a straight bowsprit projecting forward at a low angle; two masts rise from the deck, the forward mast taller, each carrying square-rigged cream-white canvas sails with visible horizontal folds when set; the ship's rail along the deck edge is dark brown rounded wood; a rope ladder of natural fibre with evenly spaced wooden rungs hangs from the starboard rail down to the waterline at the cliff side; the ship's steering wheel at the stern is a spoked wooden wheel, dark brown, eight spokes radiating from a central hub to a continuous outer ring

a single curved iron hook mounted on a short iron plate fixed to the wooden post at the edge of the ship's wheel housing; the hook curves upward and outward, shaped to hold a cylindrical object horizontally; the iron is dark grey with slight rust at the base; the hook is empty when the telescope is in use and holds ART003 when it is returned

a full-size wooden sailing vessel with a warm honey-brown hull; the bow carries a long bowsprit projecting forward at a shallow upward angle; the stern is raised above the main deck with a carved wooden rail and a large eight-spoke wooden wheel mounted at the centreline; a single tall central mast rises from the main deck and carries one wide square sail on a horizontal yard — the sail is pale cream-white and full when the wind fills it; ropes run from the masthead to the bow and to deck cleats on both sides; a wooden plank gangway can extend from the port side amidships; an iron hook is mounted on the post beside the wheel

a single-masted wooden sailing vessel about 18 metres long with a raised stern deck and a long bowsprit projecting forward at a shallow upward angle from the bow; the hull is dark brown-black weathered timber with a narrow pale cream waterline stripe; the stern is squared with a carved rail; a single tall mast rises from the centre of the deck; a large square mainsail hangs from a horizontal yard crossing the mast at right angles, the sail cream-white with a large painted golden seagull silhouette in flight at its centre — when furled the sail is bundled and lashed along the yard, when set it is taut and full; the ship's wheel is mounted on the stern deck, a wooden eight-spoke wheel with a brass hub ring that has a square recess for the compass mount; rope coils and rigging lines are present on the deck; the bowsprit carries a small triangular jib sail on a stay

a very thick rope of twisted natural-fibre strands in a warm tan-brown colour, coiled in a loose heap; one end forms a large open loop — a circle of rope roughly as wide as a child's torso — that lies flat on top of the heap or is held upright; the strands show visible twist and frayed surface fibres

A series of four flat grey stones placed in a line across a shallow, fast-moving but clearly ankle-deep mountain stream; each stone is roughly foot-sized and slightly above the water surface; the water runs visibly over and between the stones, pale blue-white with small ripples; the stream bed of pale pebbles is visible through the water
A simple red fabric lead, roughly arm-length, clipped to Nia's red collar at one end and held in Max's right hand at the other end; the lead hangs in a loose arc between hand and collar

A red child's bicycle sized for a preschool child, with two wheels, a low step-through frame, a padded red saddle, straight handlebars with red rubber grips, a small front basket mounted on the handlebars, and no training wheels; the frame is a single dominant red colour with no visible decals

A yellow child's bicycle sized for a toddler, noticeably smaller than VEH001, with two wheels, a low frame, a padded yellow saddle, short curved handlebars with yellow rubber grips, and a small front basket containing ART009 on page 1; the frame is a single dominant yellow colour

A green child's bicycle sized for a preschool child, with two wheels, a low step-through frame, a padded green saddle, straight handlebars with green rubber grips, and no front basket; the frame is a single dominant green colour

An orange child's bicycle sized for a preschool child, with two wheels, a low step-through frame, a padded orange saddle, straight handlebars with orange rubber grips, and no front basket; the frame is a single dominant orange colour

A towering Saturn V rocket approximately 110 metres tall, painted white and grey with five cylindrical stages stacked vertically. Bold black USA lettering is painted on the lower white stage. Orange and rusty-brown gantry support tower stands beside it. At launch, a column of bright orange and white flame erupts from the base, surrounded by billowing white smoke clouds. The rocket narrows slightly toward the top where the command module cone is visible. A palm-sized American flag decal is visible on the upper white section.

The Lunar Module Eagle's front descent ladder — a vertical aluminium structure about two metres tall attached to the front leg of the module, with nine horizontal rungs spaced evenly apart between two parallel vertical side rails. The ladder leads from the module's front hatch down to a circular foot-pad at the base. The module body behind it is covered in gold foil and silver panels.

A rectangular section of the Lunar Module's grey instrument console panel showing an amber warning light approximately the size of a large thumb, glowing steadily. Below it, a small rectangular illuminated altitude display readout shows a three-digit number in pale green digits. To the right, a fuel gauge with a needle indicator is mounted in a circular dial, the right quarter of the dial marked in red. A manual control stick — a forearm-length vertical handle with a T-grip at the top — is mounted centrally below the small trapezoidal front window.

A standard American flag — a rectangle of red, white, and blue with white stars on blue in the upper-left corner and alternating red and white horizontal stripes — mounted on a metal flagpole pressed into the lunar dust. A horizontal wire runs along the entire top edge of the flag, holding it fully extended and rigid in the airless environment, so the flag appears frozen mid-wave. The flagpole is silver metal, approximately one and a half metres tall.

A boxy 1960s black-and-white television set approximately 50 centimetres wide and 40 centimetres tall, mounted on a metal stand at approximately seated eye-level. The screen is a convex rectangle showing a grainy grey-toned image of a white-suited figure on a pale surface. Two rabbit-ear antennae extend from the top rear corners of the set. The cabinet is dark grey plastic with a round tuning dial on the lower right front panel.

A single sheet of thick, aged paper approximately 30 cm tall and 22 cm wide, warm amber-brown in tone with water-stained edges that fade to pale ivory at the border. The surface carries hand-drawn brown ink lines depicting a coastline along the left third, a small island silhouette at centre-right with a tiny square chest symbol marked by an X, and three curved approach lines radiating from the coast toward the island. A single line of small handwritten text in brown ink runs below the chest symbol — the letters are small but legible as a short phrase. The paper has a slight curl along the top and bottom edges. From page 9 onward the sheet appears as two separate torn pieces, both wet and darkened, the ink in the area of the path marks blurred to a grey smear.

A three-section pull-out brass telescope approximately 35 cm long when extended, warm golden-yellow in colour with a slightly tarnished surface showing brushstroke texture. The widest section at the rear is about 5 cm in diameter; each forward section steps down in diameter. The eyepiece end is capped with a small flat brass ring. The objective lens end is open. All three sections are cylindrical and align along a single straight axis.

A soft-brimmed tricorn hat with three upturned brim sections folded and stitched to form three equal points. The hat is dark green felt with a matte surface. The crown is low and rounded. The brim sections are each about 8 cm wide when flat. No feather, no badge, no buckle.

A coil of thick natural-fibre rope approximately 40 cm in diameter and 15 cm tall when laid flat, the rope itself about 3 cm thick. The colour is warm straw-yellow. The coil rests in a loose spiral of approximately eight loops. The rope surface shows a twisted three-strand weave.

A flat irregular stone approximately 15 cm wide and 10 cm tall, about 3 cm thick, pale grey with darker grey veining. One broad face carries a carved symbol: a circle with a vertical line passing through its centre from top to bottom and a short horizontal bar crossing the vertical line at the midpoint, forming a cross-within-circle motif. The edges of the stone are rough and uneven. The carved lines are approximately 4 mm wide and 2 mm deep, with raw chipped edges.

A rectangular wooden chest approximately 60 cm wide, 35 cm deep, and 35 cm tall. The wood is dark brown with visible grain. Three iron strap hinges run horizontally across the flat lid and down the front face. The lid is open, resting back against its hinges at roughly 110 degrees from horizontal. The interior is visible: a shallow layer of round gold coins and several brass instruments packed in loosely. The exterior corners are reinforced with small iron brackets. No lock visible on the front hasp.

A round flat brass compass approximately 7 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick. The case is warm golden-yellow brass with a lightly tarnished surface. The lid is open, hinged at the top, swung back flat. The inner face carries a white enamel compass rose with black cardinal markings. A thin brass needle is visible at centre, pointing slightly to the left of true north. The hinge is a small rectangular brass plate at the 12 o'clock position of the rim.

A loose gathering of round flat coins each approximately 3 cm in diameter and 3 mm thick. The colour is warm yellow-gold. The coin surfaces show faint relief markings that are weathered and illegible. The coins sit in a shallow pile inside the chest and in two separated groupings on the stone beside it.

A rolled cloth flag approximately 40 cm long and 6 cm in diameter when rolled. The cloth is white with a broad red diagonal stripe running from one corner to the opposite corner, visible only at the unrolled ends where a few centimetres of fabric hang loose. The roll is held by a single loose loop of thin cord.

A large hardcover book approximately 35 cm tall and 25 cm wide, lying open flat on a reading stand. The cover boards are dark brown leather with worn edges. Both pages visible are covered in dense columns of small printed text in black ink, the individual words illegible at reading distance. The back inside cover pocket, visible at the lower right when the book lies open, holds the folded map — one amber-brown corner of paper protrudes about 3 cm above the pocket edge.

A handheld brass instrument approximately 20 cm long. Two straight brass arms of equal length are joined at one end by a single pivot screw, allowing them to open and close like a wide V. Each arm is flat, about 1.5 cm wide and 3 mm thick, with a row of small engraved degree markings along one edge. The surface is warm golden-yellow brass, lightly tarnished, with visible brushstroke texture on the painted surface.

A single-masted wooden sailing vessel approximately 15 metres long with a broad hull. The hull planks are dark brown with a single wide yellow painted stripe running along the full length at the top of the hull, just below the rail. The name GOLDENE MÖWE is painted in yellow block letters on the dark brown bow. One tall wooden mast rises from the centre of the deck. A single large square sail hangs from a horizontal wooden yard: the sail is white cotton with a painted black silhouette of a flying seagull at its centre. The deck planks are unpainted grey-brown wood. A wooden ship's wheel with eight spokes stands at the stern. A narrow wooden gangway plank connects the port side midship rail to the riverbank when moored. The stern carries a small carved wooden gull figure as a figurehead on the transom.

A two-masted wooden sailing vessel slightly longer and narrower than the Goldene Möwe, with a sleeker hull. The hull is painted black overall. Two tall wooden masts carry large triangular fore-and-aft sails in deep charcoal grey, almost black. No name visible on the hull at the distances shown. The sails are always taut and full, giving the impression of speed. Seen at distance as a small dark shape on the horizon or across the water.

a palm-sized circular disc of bright silver metal, flush-mounted into the dark grain of the Holzbrücke's wooden support beam just above the waterline. Its surface is smooth and slightly convex. Around its outer edge runs a ring of tiny carved capital letters — the arc of text reads: BOTH TOGETHER, OR NEITHER TRULY — spaced evenly in a full circle. The disc catches light in a warm golden way that does not quite match the colour of the afternoon sun. No clasp, no hinge; it is pressed entirely flat into the wood.

A single large scale roughly the size of an open adult hand, oval in outline with a pointed tip at the bottom and a slightly curved flat top edge where it once attached to the wing. The surface carries the same deep forest-green base colour as the dragon's body with ochre-gold undertones that catch warm light. The texture is smooth with faint concentric ring markings pressed into the surface. The edges are slightly translucent at the very rim in a warm amber wash. No metallic shine — rendered in warm watercolour pigment.

Words carved directly into rough pale grey limestone, the letters chiselled in an uneven hand. The text is carved in two short lines. The carving reads — in weathered Swiss German — a sentence stating that two guardians on the neighbouring peak hold the scale. The carved grooves are deep and shadow-filled, giving each letter a dark recessed line against the lighter stone face. Surrounding stone surface is rough and pitted with natural texture.

A small rectangular scrap of cream-white paper, slightly crumpled at one corner. On its surface are a few short lines of handwritten words copied in a child's unsteady hand — the letters are small and loosely formed. The writing is legible as written text but individual words are not quoted. The paper is plain with no border or lines.

A round inflatable rubber ball, roughly the size of Julian's torso. The ball is solid orange with no pattern, seams or print. Its surface is smooth and slightly shiny in a warm watercolour wash. When in the water it sits high, floating with about half its volume above the surface.

A rectangular flat plank of rough-hewn pale brown timber mounted horizontally on a single vertical wooden post. The post is driven into stony ground. The plank face shows a row of five simple symbols carved into the wood — geometric shapes including a circle, a triangle, two parallel horizontal lines, and a cross — arranged left to right in a single row. No letters or numbers appear on the sign. The carved symbols are dark-shadowed against the lighter wood grain.

A knee-high rounded boulder of light grey granite sitting at a fork in the trail. Three flat arrow shapes are carved in shallow relief into its front face, each pointing in a different direction — one to the left, one straight ahead, one to the right. The carvings are simple and bold, with shadow-filled grooves. The stone surface is rough and lichen-spotted in pale yellowish-green.

A wide gate made of two vertical planks of dark weathered brown timber joined by three horizontal crossbars, forming two rectangular panel sections side by side. The gate is hinged on the left side to a stone post and closes against a matching stone post on the right. A square iron lock box is mounted at waist height on the right-hand plank. When closed the gate blocks the path entirely. When open, both planks swing left, leaving the path clear.

A small child-sized backpack in plain green canvas with two padded shoulder straps and a single main compartment closed by a top zip. No logos or prints. The body is a simple rounded rectangular shape, slightly bulging at the centre. Worn on Levin's back at all times except when he sets it down at the cave wall.

A large round boulder of rough mid-grey granite, roughly as tall as Max's shoulders when he stands beside it. Its surface is uneven and pitted with natural texture. In the scene after Max has pushed it, the boulder sits to one side of the stone path, a scrape mark visible in the pale dirt where it rolled.

A child-sized bicycle with a red frame, two round wheels with dark rubber tyres and silver spokes, a low saddle at child hip height, straight handlebars with red rubber grips, and a small dark saddle bag behind the seat. The frame is a simple diamond shape scaled for a preschool-aged child. No training wheels.

A very small child-sized bicycle with a yellow frame scaled for a toddler, two round wheels with dark rubber tyres and silver spokes, a very low saddle at toddler hip height, and short upright handlebars with yellow rubber grips. The frame is a simple step-through shape. No training wheels — Julian is old enough to manage a balance bike.

A child-sized bicycle with a blue frame, two round wheels with dark rubber tyres and silver spokes, a low saddle at child hip height, and straight handlebars with blue rubber grips. The frame is a simple diamond shape scaled for a preschool-aged child. No training wheels.

A child-sized bicycle with an orange frame, two round wheels with dark rubber tyres and silver spokes, a low saddle at child hip height, and straight handlebars with orange rubber grips. The frame is a simple diamond shape scaled for a preschool-aged child. No training wheels.

a small irregular shard roughly the size of a child's palm, curved slightly like a broken roof tile, warm teal-green on the outer surface with a faint golden sheen from pooled pigment, pale amber on the concave inner face, edges jagged and uneven, no text

a single large scale roughly the size of an adult hand, oval with one straight clipped base edge and a smoothly rounded top, warm teal-green on the convex outer surface with visible paint-granulation texture, pale amber on the concave inner face, edges clean and firm, fits flush over the bare patch on the dragon's wing

words cut directly into rough pale grey limestone on the interior cave wall at child chest-height, the carved grooves dark with shadow, lettering appears as weathered chiselled marks — illegible to the viewer but Levin reads them; no separate plaque or frame, the text is part of the raw cave wall surface

a single rough-hewn wooden post planted vertically in the ground with three flat rectangular wooden arm boards attached horizontally at the top, each arm pointing in a different direction — left, centre and right; the arms are unpainted weathered pale brown timber; each arm has weathered carved text that is illegible at reading distance; the post stands at chest-height to a preschool child

a low rectangular chest carved from pale grey granite, roughly knee-height to an adult, as wide as two children standing side by side; a flat slab lid rests on top when closed; the lid is hinged at the back with two visible dark iron bands; the outer surface is rough-hewn with visible chisel marks; no lock visible on the exterior; no text

a low gate spanning a narrow path, made of two vertical rough timber planks connected by two horizontal cross-rails — one near the top, one near the bottom — forming a simple rectangular frame; the gate swings on two dark iron strap hinges fixed to a timber post on the left; the top cross-rail has words carved along its length in shallow chisel cuts that are illegible at viewing distance; the gate stands open, swung to the right, with the path visible beyond

a round rubber ball roughly the size of a toddler's torso, solid yellow with a single broad white horizontal band around its equator, slightly shiny surface rendered with visible brushwork highlights, used as a floating aid in the brook scene

a child-sized two-wheeled bicycle sized for a preschooler; frame painted red; two black rubber-tyred wheels of equal size; a low handlebar with red rubber grips; a padded black saddle on an adjustable seat post; no training wheels; a simple black chain guard over the rear sprocket

a small two-wheeled balance bicycle sized for a toddler, noticeably smaller than Levin's bicycle; frame painted yellow; two black rubber-tyred wheels; a low handlebar with yellow rubber grips; a padded black saddle on a low seat post; no pedals, no chain, no chain guard — a balance bike only

a child-sized two-wheeled bicycle sized for a preschooler; frame painted blue; two black rubber-tyred wheels of equal size; a low handlebar with blue rubber grips; a padded black saddle on an adjustable seat post; no training wheels; a simple black chain guard over the rear sprocket

a child-sized two-wheeled bicycle sized for a preschooler; frame painted green; two black rubber-tyred wheels of equal size; a low handlebar with green rubber grips; a padded black saddle on an adjustable seat post; no training wheels; a simple black chain guard over the rear sprocket
A palm-sized envelope of thick brown kraft paper, sealed on the back flap with a round disk of dark red wax bearing a simple pressed cross impression; the front face is blank.

A fist-sized sheet of cream-coloured paper with hand-inked black lines representing the lanes and streets of Baden Altstadt; three small red-ink cross marks indicate locations; a compass rose is drawn in the lower-right corner.

A carved rectangular stone panel set into the front face of the fountain basin, approximately forearm-length wide; it depicts a simple heraldic shield with a diagonal band carved in low relief, worn smooth by weather.
A small white paper envelope, slightly damp and crinkled, about palm-sized, with the names 'Lily & Ethan' written in black ink on the front; no seal, flap tucked in.

A hand-bound book approximately A5 size with a soft cream fabric cover decorated with small hand-drawn flowers in pencil; its pages are filled with printed photographs and handwritten captions in blue ink; lying open on a stone surface.

a chest-height stack of round split birch logs, pale cream-white wood faces visible, stacked neatly in a rectangular formation approximately one metre wide and one metre tall, set on bare packed earth

a large bright green farm tractor with enormous round knobby rear wheels approximately twice the height of a child, a flat rectangular metal engine hood, a black vertical exhaust pipe rising from the front of the engine hood, a wide flat metal seat with a steering wheel on a column, and smaller front wheels; the bodywork is green with yellow detailing on the wheel hubs
a mid-sized dark blue school backpack with yellow zipper pulls and two front pockets, lying on a wooden floor

a small square piece of white paper folded in half twice to a palm-sized rectangle, slightly creased at the edges, with handwritten black ink text reading 'Wer hilft, der findet' visible on the outer fold of the first note; subsequent notes show only folded white paper, text on the inside
a tall unstable stack of mixed household laundry — towels, T-shirts, a pair of jeans — approximately arm-height, carried in both arms, with the top item beginning to slide

a rectangular wooden dining table with a plain white cotton tablecloth, four ceramic plates in cream white, four clear glass tumblers, and stainless steel cutlery (fork on the left, knife and spoon on the right) neatly arranged at each place setting
a palm-sized square children's picture book with a bright orange cover showing a cartoon animal; slightly worn corners
a fist-sized shallow ceramic bowl in terracotta orange, rough-textured on the outside, smooth on the inside, filled with clear water; small enough for a tortoise to step into

a well-worn small brown plush teddy bear roughly the size of a forearm from elbow to wrist, with a stitched black nose, small round black button eyes, and slightly matted fur from years of use; no accessories
a loose heap of children's clothing — several colourful T-shirts, a pair of shorts, a hoodie — piled approximately knee-height on a bedroom floor
irregular pale grey cobblestones set in fan-shaped patterns on a narrow lane or bridge surface, slightly worn smooth from centuries of foot traffic, warm summer light catching the rounded stone edges

a small chalk cross drawn on a pale sandstone paving tile — two short strokes each roughly a palm-width long forming a simple cross — white chalk against pale grey stone, the lines slightly dusty at the edges

a solid wooden bench with dark green painted slat seat and backrest, supported by two ornate black cast-iron legs with curved scroll detailing; the gap between the ground and the lowest bench slat is approximately one hand-span high

a small rectangular wooden crate roughly the size of a shoebox, made of light pine with visible wood grain, tied shut with a thin natural-fibre cord knotted on top; the lid lifts off with the cord removed
a round hard-candy lollipop roughly the size of a large coin, on a straight white paper stick approximately finger-length; one is cherry red, one is blueberry blue, both with a slight glossy sheen

a palm-sized unfolded sheet of white paper with neat handwritten blue ink text, held flat open; the text reads 'Liebe Detektive. Die Schnitzeljagd hat funktioniert, weil ihr alle mitgemacht habt.' with further lines below
stainless steel cutlery (forks, spoons, knives), cream ceramic plates, and a large silver aluminium pasta pot with a lid; the pot is approximately the size of a small bucket with two side handles

a small rectangular printed photograph roughly the size of a playing card, showing a tidied apartment interior — a neatly set dining table, an orderly room, and a full tortoise water dish — printed on glossy photo paper

a single sheet of thick, cream-coloured paper roughly the size of two open hands placed side by side, edges ragged and slightly curled; the left half shows dense hand-drawn coastlines, depth-sounding marks and compass rose in dark brown ink, all lines crisp; the right half is a pale wash of faded brown where the ink has run and spread into the paper fibre, only ghost outlines of lines remaining; no legible text anywhere on the map, all markings are weathered symbols and curves

a rectangular wooden chest roughly knee-height and arm's-length wide, dark brown wood with visible grain, iron corner brackets at all eight corners, a flat domed lid hinged at the back; the lid stands fully open, resting back on its hinges; the interior visible from the front shows a warm golden glow of coins and objects packed inside; an iron hasp clasp hangs open at the front centre of the lid

a single brass telescope in three pull-out cylindrical sections, each section slightly narrower than the last toward the eyepiece end; fully extended to roughly forearm length; surface is dull gold-toned brass with faint surface marks; the wide objective end has a dark circular lens opening, the narrow eyepiece end is smooth and rounded

a single wooden oar roughly twice the height of a person, pale natural wood with a long cylindrical shaft widening at one end into a flat broad blade shaped like an elongated oval; the shaft shows scuff marks; the blade end sticks out from a heap of gear at an upward diagonal angle

a large rectangular slab of grey stone set flush into a cave wall, roughly twice the height of a person and one person's arm-span wide; the surface is flat with four carved pictures arranged in a single horizontal row across the centre: from left to right, a wave shape, a bird in flight, a key shape, and a boat shape; each carving is a shallow relief, approximately hand-sized, evenly spaced across the width of the slab; the door shows a faint vertical seam down its left edge where it meets the cave wall

a standard digging shovel with a long straight wooden handle, pale brown wood, and a flat squared metal blade at the lower end mounted perpendicular to the handle shaft; the metal blade is dark grey iron with a slightly curved lower edge for digging; handle length roughly equal to a person's height

a wooden sailing boat roughly ten metres long with a single mast rising from the centre of the deck; the hull is dark brown painted wood sitting low in the water; a large square-cut sail is rigged on a horizontal yard mounted at right angles to the mast and hangs from it, the sail fabric cream-white with a simple black painted shape of crossed bones at its centre; the bow is blunt and rounded; a rope railing runs along each side of the deck attached to short wooden posts; the stern has a flat rail where a figure can stand at the tiller

a wooden sailing boat of similar length to the Goldene Möwe but with a slightly narrower hull and a taller single mast; the hull is painted dark grey; the sail is a tall triangular lateen sail rigged from the mast on a long diagonal yard, the sail fabric plain off-white with no markings; the bow is sharper and more pointed than the Goldene Möwe; seen mostly at a distance as a small fast shape on the water
A small folded paper city map, roughly palm-sized when folded, printed with street grids and place names in black ink on pale cream paper, creased along four fold lines into a neat rectangular packet

A palm-sized toothbrush with a straight white handle and soft pink bristles; slightly smaller than ART002 in total length; the handle has a rounded end and a light pink rubber grip band near the base

Several large transparent plastic shopping bags (cornets) with flat handles, filled with market produce — one shows the pale crust end of a baguette poking out the top, another shows the tops of green herbs, a third shows a small round red tomato near the top

A short palm-sized toothpaste tube, white plastic with a blue and white label, a screw cap at the narrow end; the tube is slightly squeezed in the middle from use
A palm-sized old worn toothbrush with a slightly yellowed white handle and faded dark green bristles that are bent outward at the tips from extended use; the handle has a small chip near the base

The lowest step of a wooden residential staircase — a broad flat wooden tread with a rounded front edge, painted white on the riser, the tread itself in pale natural wood, wide enough for an adult to sit on comfortably

A small round digital sport watch on a black rubber strap, worn on the left wrist; the face is dark grey with a bright green digital display showing a running countdown timer; two small side buttons visible on the case edge

A single-scoop ice cream cone — the scoop is pale rose-pink strawberry, roughly fist-sized, sitting on a pointed waffle cone forearm-length from tip to scoop; the surface of the scoop is smooth and slightly glistening
